clue.text: East End believers go for hard work

indicators.note: Cockney speech of London's East End drops the initial aitch, so the believers lose their opening letter

parts.note: Hindus are believers in Hinduism
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Religious folk in London's East End swap faith for a spell of graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' tells you to drop the H as a Cockney would, so HINDUS becomes INDUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry can mean diligence, sustained hard labour, as in a person of great industry.

clue.text: Informal, frivolous kind of movie

parts.note: dictionaries abbreviate informal as inf.
light, as in light entertainment, means frivolous

explanation.surface: A casual, throwaway sort of film.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-flight film is the sort shown to passengers on an aeroplane.

clue.text: Police officer employing skill in board game

indicators.note: the officer takes on, or holds, the skill, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A detective uses his talents playing a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is played by throwing at a dartboard, so it is literally a game with a board.

clue.text: Gurgling noise to suppress almost completely during school

indicators.note: the trimmed verb comes in the course of the school, so it goes inside it
all but the last letter of the verb is kept

parts.note: to quell is to suppress

explanation.surface: A school tries to stifle some gurgling racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' drops the last letter of the verb; 'during' puts what remains within the school abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A squelch is the wet sucking sound of feet in mud, a gurgling noise.

clue.text: Study in Scarlet, A

indicators.note: the letter A is placed in the colour

parts.note: scarlet is a bright red

explanation.surface: Mimics the Sherlock Holmes title A Study in Scarlet, oddly punctuated.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma breaks the famous title: 'Study' is the definition, then A goes in scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject, especially at a British university, is to study it.

clue.text: Grasps experience with drug is a warning to slow down

parts.note: slang for seeing through them, grasping what they are up to
a trip is an experience on hallucinogens

explanation.surface: Someone who understands drug-taking knows it signals a need to ease off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumble strip is a ridged band across a road that vibrates tyres to alert drivers to brake.

clue.text: Opens international naval force?

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, is the international body
the SEALs are the US Navy's special forces

explanation.surface: A question about a multinational navy that 'opens'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseal a letter or document is to break it open.

clue.text: Rural event's place to drink riotously and neck, mostly

parts.note: a bar is where drinks are served

indicators.note: in riotous disorder, so the letters are jumbled
most of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A country do held where people drink rowdily and kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is the verb to kiss, but here it is only fodder: 'mostly' loses its K and 'riotously' shuffles it with 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn dance is a country social with folk dancing, often held in a barn.

clue.text: Dab's no longer fresh

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
fresh can mean cheeky, pert

explanation.surface: A dab, the fish, has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dab' looks like the flatfish; it is a dab hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab, or dab hand, is a skilled person, a specialist.

clue.text: Unimaginative motor-racing clubs

parts.note: Formula I (Formula One) is the top motor-racing series
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on car-racing clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something following a set recipe is stale and lacking originality.

clue.text: Muse about rise of evil couple disregarding the odds

parts.note: CA, circa, means about

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ill means evil, as in ill deeds

indicators.note: ignore the odd-placed letters and keep the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone pondering the ascent of a wicked pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns ILL into LLI; 'disregarding the odds' keeps OPE from couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope was the Greek Muse of epic poetry.

clue.text: See 5
Slight loss at end of this month and last one

indicators.note: the final letter goes from the abbreviation

parts.note: inst., instant, means of this month in old business letters
ult., ultimo, means of last month

explanation.surface: A small dip at the end of this month and the previous one.
explanation.walkthrough: inst. and ult. are old commercial-letter abbreviations for this month and last month; 'loss at end of' clips the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub, an insult; both nouns work.

clue.text: Bush's expression of approval accompanied by hesitation

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cheer of approval
and means together with
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: President Bush's halting way of signalling approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the president; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a poisonous evergreen flowering shrub.

clue.text: Trouble with heel? Put 'Cobblers' on this

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
a ship that heels leans over, or lists

explanation.surface: A broken shoe heel, and a dismissive 'cobblers' in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense; here it is an errand: take the shoe to the cobbler's.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder of errands, on which one might write 'cobblers' to get a heel mended.

clue.text: Eccentrically-constructed airport without terminal rejects third of drones

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, punning on an airport terminal

parts.note: Heathrow is London's main airport
to bin something is to reject it

indicators.note: the middle pair of six letters is the central third of the word

explanation.surface: An airport that lacks a terminal and turns away drones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without terminal' trims HEATHROW; 'third of' takes ON, the middle third of DRONES.
explanation.definitionFit: W. Heath Robinson drew absurdly complicated contraptions, so his name describes overelaborate machines.

clue.text: Fighting that erupts involving kingmaker but not Conservative king

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the trimmed name
an eruption throws the letters about
the following letters are removed

parts.note: the Earl of Warwick was known as the Kingmaker in the Wars of the Roses
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Conflict breaks out over a royal power-broker, though not a Tory monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupts' scrambles 'that' around the kingmaker, who loses C and K as signalled by 'but not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two parties at war with each other are in conflict.

clue.text: Ass pulled up two-thirds of the way through eating sweet plant

indicators.note: the reversed animal swallows the sweet word
in a down clue, pulling up reads the letters bottom to top
four of the six letters are kept, the last third dropped

parts.note: a donkey is an ass
twee means sweet, cloyingly so

explanation.surface: A donkey hauled upwards midway while munching a sweet plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds of the way through' cuts DONKEY to DONK; 'pulled up' gives KNOD, which eats TWEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotweed, especially Japanese knotweed, is an invasive weed with jointed stems.

clue.text: Batting averages, possibly, that might be seen on cup

definitions.text: Batting averages, possibly, that might be seen on cup

parts.words: Batting averages, possibly, that might be seen on cup
parts.note: willow is the wood of cricket bats, and a run of averages forms a pattern, so a bat's pattern is jokingly the china design

explanation.surface: A cricketer's statistics might be printed on a trophy cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup' suggests a sporting trophy but is a teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue Chinese-style design of bridge, birds and trees is common on English china.

clue.text: Adult avoiding inappropriate liaison before end of village fête

indicators.note: inappropriate suggests letters out of their proper places
the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An adult steers clear of an improper affair before a village fête ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes one A from LIAISON; 'inappropriate' jumbles LIISON into LIONIS. 'fête' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fête someone is to celebrate and honour them as a celebrity.

clue.text: Slogan has Liberal in a stew

indicators.note: the party letter goes in the dish

parts.note: a tagine is a North African stew

explanation.surface: A politician's catchphrase lands a Liberal in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' looks like the idiom for trouble; the stew is a tagine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagline is a catchphrase used in advertising.

clue.text: Thin pieces of wood on top of earth

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: spars are poles of wood such as masts

explanation.surface: Slender timbers laid over soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means scanty or thinly spread.

clue.text: Occasional table, kind of?

definitions.meaning: happening at intervals, from time to time
the chart of chemical elements is a table of this sort

explanation.surface: An occasional table is a small side table; the clue asks if this is one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasional table' looks like the furniture; split it: 'Occasional' and 'table, kind of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurring at intervals means now and then; and the chemists' element chart bears this name.

clue.text: Horrified at abandoning Christie on street

indicators.note: in an across clue, the first piece comes before the next
the word at leaves the name

parts.note: Agatha Christie, the crime novelist

explanation.surface: Appalled at deserting Agatha Christie in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes AT from AGATHA, leaving AGHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with horror or amazement.

clue.text: Native American leaving husband swiftly

indicators.note: the letter departs from the tribe's name

parts.note: an Apache is a Native American

explanation.surface: A Native American walks out on her husband in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old word for quickly, at speed.

clue.text: Honest regret follows deed lacking in tact

indicators.note: the regret comes after, in a down clue below
the synonym is taken out of the word tact

parts.note: an act is a deed
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Genuine remorse after a tactless act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' removes ACT from TACT, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: True means sincere, truthful and faithful.

clue.text: International winter sportsman perhaps heading off back for massage

indicators.note: the letters are read in reverse
the first letter is removed

parts.note: a skier is one example of a winter sportsman

explanation.surface: A beheaded international skier heads back for a rubdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' trims SKIER to KIER; 'back' reverses IKIER to REIKI.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiki is a Japanese healing therapy using touch, a kind of massage.

clue.text: Finish one semester every four years, according to report?

indicators.note: report means something heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: with two semesters a year, one term in every eight terms

explanation.surface: A student wonders about one term each quadrennium.
explanation.walkthrough: Four years hold eight semesters, so one semester is 'term in eight'.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to an end.

clue.text: Local newspaper journalist rang

parts.note: Echo is a common British local paper title, e.g. the Liverpool Echo
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter on the local paper telephoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rang' looks like phoned; it means resounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that rang out, reverberating, repeated itself.

clue.text: Did umpire upset Federer, giving point in?

indicators.note: the compass point goes inside
upset scrambles the letters of the tennis star's name

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Did the official rattle Federer by awarding a point?
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FEDERER into REFERED, with E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To referee a match is to umpire it, to judge it.
